DeElf 1000 Bulk Clear Card Sleeves for Playing Card Standard Size Trading Game Fit MTG Baseball and Sport Cards Acid Free Enhance Penny Protector There are many factors in picking the right sleeves for your favorite card games: How do they feel? How do they fit? Are they consistent? How do they shuffle? Are they too slick to stay stacked? Do they add too much thickness and bulk? Do they poof-out and add even more thickness to a stack? Are they expensive? Do they have a ridiculous holograph? LOL
I considered all these things as I tried sleeves from BCW, Fantasy Flight, Ultra-Pro, Mayday, and the Chinese generic brands. The sleeve that excelled in all these criteria were from the Delphia set for Gloomhaven, but when I went to buy more, they were discontinued! Arrrugh! I sent an Amazon message to the distributor from my previous order, and was told the Panda sleeves were from the same company. My sets of 1000 sleeves arrived today and I am thrilled! They are the same material, with the same qualities of thin, close-fitting protection, that are not too slick to stack well, and not too matt to shuffle beautifully. And to top it off, the Panda sleeves are 1mm narrower than the Delphia sleeves and so the fit, for games like Arkham Horror LCG, is even better! (see photo) Absolutely my favorite sleeves, by far! The bonus card boxes, with their handy roll of double-sided modeler's tape, is a friendly gesture. Five Stars.
text_fidelity_b: DeElf 1000 Bulk Clear Card Sleeves for Playing Card Standard Size Trading Game Fit MTG Baseball and Sport Cards Acid Free Enhance Penny Protector

text_fidelity_a:
Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches First thing I noticed was how close this stuffed goose resembled the real thing. Second, the sound effect was so realistic. And third, there was no way for the batteries to be removed. All three demands of mine has been met. Now I purchase a lot of duck and geese related items for the baby shower of my niece, my brother finally got a girl who though he was decent and good looking enough to reproduce with. So while I was confused on what Auntie of the year was going to give to my first born niece, I remembered all the years growing up where my brother tormented and made fun of. Then it dawned on me! I was going to gift all duck and geese related things to my niece so she will grow up loving them. Why you ask? Well I will share a story. Long ago, back in the mid 90’s my grandmother took my brother and I to the local duck pond to let us feed the ducks bread. I, obviously the intelligent one, knew to throw the bread as far away as I could away from me. My brother, a few fries short of a happy meal, threw it at his feet. Before he knew it all these mystical, beautiful beasts of the pond surrounded him. I remember him mocking me, “ you aren’t cool the ducks don’t like you”. And I can remember clearly him saying “ I AM THEIR GOD.” Then karma happened. All my Sunday school teaching happened as I sat in the car with my grandmother waiting for this false duck god to finish his loaf of bread it happened. Our almighty creater from above, the real God, spoke “There is no true God but me” and just like that my brother ran out of bed. These geese, realized he had no bread and he was a false prophet started to chant their battle cry! Next thing I knew, my brother started to get attacked by a mob of geese. Now he’s banging at my grandmother’s car door to let him in but she still laughing so hard she couldn’t reach over to unlock the door. (We didn’t have power doors during this time) I could of easily reached over and unlocked the door, but I sat back and watched this biblical lesson unfold in front of my eyes. Did you know geese have teeth on their tongue? He found out that day Eventually my grandma let him in and they surrounded the car for a good 10 minutes before they left to stalk their new prey.
That day I almost became an only child and that day changed my brother forever.

So yes this stuffed geese and all the other geese and duck related items from this seller is worth the money. It was amazing seeing a grown mad cowering in fear as he unwrapped every single duck and goose at his baby shower. His child is going to befriend the very creatures that almost murdered him in cold blood over a loaf of bread.
10/10 will buy from again.
text_fidelity_b: Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Cars Playset, 4-Level Toy Garage & Tow Truck in 1:64 Scale, Kid-Powered Elevator, Car Repair Station & Spiral Ramp For my 4 and a half year old grandson. He loves his cars and so this was a nice compact "repair garage" play structure. It will not be something you will want to break down daily and store, it will need to be up and available for immediate play. It will stay at my house for his visits and be stored on a closet shelf between visits. It came with one little tow truck vehicle. There is no car storage; this is just a play activity. A turning knob on top of the elevator brings cars up to individual floor levels and there are gates on the ramps that divert the cars to a car maintenance floor and a car wash floor in the structure. Although it says it's 4 level, there is nothing but a ramp from the elevator on the upper level and the lower level is really just the entry to the elevator and an open accessible area underneath that the imagination can invent a use for.

The instructions were also less than stellar and being only in black and white, identifying some of the little pieces was sometimes guesswork. There are small pieces that can be pulled off, so observe the recommended age group for this toy. We were not interested in all the many decorative stickers that can be applied on this toy, so only used what we wanted to.

It appears to be sturdy enough and, if incorporated with some other play structures, could keep his attention for a lengthy period of play time.
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Cars Playset, 4-Level Toy Garage & Tow Truck in 1:64 Scale, Kid-Powered Elevator, Car Repair Station & Spiral Ramp

Adora Belle 18-inch Doll, Amazing Girls Sweater Weather Sam (Amazon Exclusive) One of the things that I love about the Adora dolls is that each doll has her own face sculpt. The dolls look unique and not like clones with different skin tones and face paint.

The body composition also has a difference over the American Girl or Playtime by Eimmie dolls. There’s a neck joint and the neck, shoulder, and upper torso area is plastic while the lower torso is cloth. This allows for a greater range of neck & head motion over other dolls of this size, which have completely cloth torsos and limited, if any, neck motion.

Her clothing is designed with play in mind, making it easy for an older child to take on and off, but the quality is such that she would make an excellent addition to a collector’s display as well.

Her red hair is a brilliant color and her freckles are a nice detail.

WOW! Stuff Collection Fantastic Beasts – Newt’s Light Painting Wand – Award Winner! You will open up a huge world of fun with the Wizarding World WW-1024 Harry Potter's Light Painting Wand, Brown. The Harry Potter wand is about 14 inches long with a grainy wood looking black handle and brown wand part that ends with a very bright LED light tip. The wand has a nice feel and weight to it and seems to be made of a strong resin plastic. The wand comes in a lovely window box with directions, customer support information and a bonus app for making your light paintings.

There is a tiny button on the wand’s handle for turning on the LED light which only stays on as long as you hold the button down. The 3 included 1.5 V LR41 batteries are replaceable by opening the handle end with a phillips screwdriver. This is a great thing, as I can see replacing the batteries often, as our kids can’t put this wand down for a minute. For those of you that look forward to some creative light painting, you will want to download the app. Light painting is just photographing a moving light at a longer exposure shutter speed, in the dark, with no flash. You will want the camera on a tripod to get the light design without shaky movement.

In our house, we can’t get the kids to stop playing with the light painting wand long enough for us to try the light painting. Of course we had to buy another wand, as they play Tag with each other in the dark as well as hide and seek in the dark and casting spells on each other- endless fun for them. I just got one of the wands after bedtime to try a bit of light painting. I only used my camera on the Slow Shutter dial, did not have time to set up a tripod, and snapped a couple photos in the dark with no flash. I caught a photo of the wand making a “V”, and it came out nice for no app or tripod yet. I have seen light painting photos that are fantastic when you know how to manually set your camera for long exposures. Adding a colored cellophane over the light tip makes for gorgeous colored lights too. Our kids love playing with these wands and could care less about the light painting for now. These wands are getting a lot of playtime and are a huge hit- especially with Halloween around the corner. 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: WOW! Stuff Collection Fantastic Beasts – Newt’s Light Painting Wand – Award Winner!

If they come up with an additional iteration that can hang on a wall, or with the option to buy more shelves then yay great. (I was fully prepared to spend money to get this to work for me and my fam) Otherwise this kind of misses the mark for the cost.

Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game I was really excited about this product, as Pictionary is one of my all-time favorite party games. This was a disappointment on so many levels.

First, there is no storage box. It comes with a frame, a frame stand, a timer, and a marker. And a dice, which got lost in no time. The "frame" itself is about the size of a sheet of paper (8" by 10"), and it is clear, so you can see through it. The small size makes it ideal for travel or a backpack, but the fact that it is clear makes it difficult to see when holding it on your lap. And forget about using it on the black coffee table. It works much better when used flat, on a light background surface. I like that you can use the frame as a window, so the see-through feature may be useful one at a time. It's pretty much impossible for two people to write on opposite sides of the board at the same time. Honestly it is pretty much for anyone to write on the board when it is in the stand, which keeps the board vertical.

We like to use large dry-erase boards when we pay Pictionary. I would recommend that rather than this game. The frame might be fun to draw on once in a while -- but shy not get a small whiteboard, which is much better suited for the purpose?

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game [[VIDEOID:8f653ee987e2df8b52e209e097da8a22]] This is such a cool game! It's a scaled down version of Monopoly, and each game only takes 5-15 minutes to play, instead of the hours of a regular Monopoly game. So you'll hear something with this Monopoly game that you won't hear with any other Monopoly game, which is "Want to play again?"

It still captures the essence of Monopoly, so it still feels like a Monopoly game. It's more of a social game than a strategy game, but that will make it more fun for more people.

They've taken out the property cards, and replaced them with little tiles and a tower. The number of tiles, not the original value of the tile, determine how much that you pay when you land on someone else's property. The old Community Chest cards are now Empire cards, and you get a couple to hold on to at the start of the game, and you can use these strategically, and do various combos with them.

It's very fun, and I liked it a lot. If you get just one game this year, this should be the game you pick.

Pros:
+Excellent instructions
+Extremely well designed
+Has cool brands like Fender, Nerf, and Coke
+Quick version of Monopoly (I never thought I'd ever use quick and Monopoly in the same sentence.)
+They did an awesome job of play testing this game. It's very balanced and very fun. Whoever worked on the team that made this game should be promoted.

Cons:
-Less strategy than regular Monopoly, but it is more fun for more people
-Because it's subsidized by advertising, they really should be giving this game away. But, the advertising isn't as annoying as in other games.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a: Force1 U45W FPV Drone with Camera for Adults - VR Ready Quadcopter RTF Remote Control Drone with 720p HD Wide Angle Drone Camera, 6 Axis Gyro, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, and 2 Drone Batteries I was so excited to get this drone.  I have flown a pretty nice professional DJI but knew this would not be the same.  It arrived on time and in excellent shape.  First problem was there was only 2 batteries (supposed to be 3).  I charged the batteries (in the garbage charger).  I tried to charge them in my B6 charger but it ready low cell voltage- I should have known then there was an issue.  After assembling everything I took it out and followed the directions to calibrate and sync the drone.  It started up and rose up about 10 feet and started drifting to the right no matter what I did.  I landed it and recalibrated and had the same results.  Then the low battery beeping started.  I landed and changed out batteries (total flight time was less than 5 mins).  The second battery would not even turn on the lights.  Recharged the first battery and in 3 mins the drone crashed with a dead battery.  Charged the second battery again and no go.  So frustrated and disappointed.  I packed it all up and put in for a return.  There are a lot of websites that HIGHLY recommend this drone- I have a feeling they are paid for this as this thing is truly unusable.  The trim functions don't do a darn thing and the batteries are horrible.  Thanks to Amazon for a great hassle free return.
text_fidelity_b: Force1 U45W FPV Drone with Camera for Adults - VR Ready Quadcopter RTF Remote Control Drone with 720p HD Wide Angle Drone Camera, 6 Axis Gyro, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, and 2 Drone Batteries

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys My Giant Busy Box Craft Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity I'm not the best at doing any kind of organized crafts with my children. My style is more along the lines of giving them art supplies and letting them create what they want, and honestly, that's what I'll always prefer for them. They really enjoy projects that have a somewhat defined end result sometimes, though, and so it's kits like this that come to my rescue. Thankfully, they still get to be a bit creative with these projects, and while end results might look similar for many children, they probably won't look just alike.

There are 16 projects within this box, with lots and lots of little pieces. There are only instructions for 5 of the projects, but really, with those instructions, you can easily figure out the rest of them. I would have preferred for each of the projects to have been individually packaged to make things easier. I have had kits like that, and they make things a breeze for this disorganized mama. This kit does need a bit more organization on my part, but it's really not that bad. The supplies are all separated into different bags, and there are even extra bags for me to divide out some of the supplies. I could turn my children loose with everything and see what they come up with, but I prefer separating each project(at least for the most part), so that my children can choose which one they want to do, and not worry about running out of supplies before all the project are finished. Between my 3 children, I'll get 5 rainy days out of this box, with one extra. (I can't beat that!) ;) Plus, the included finger crayons can be used after all the projects are finished.

This is a really nice box of crafts. Especially if you're like me, and don't do so well with organized crafts, this is an excellent way to give your children some fun with crafts.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys My Giant Busy Box Craft Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity

text_fidelity_a:
Syma X5C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Explorers Quad Copter w/ Camera After getting an X12 over Christmas, and having an absolute blast crashing into everything while learning to fly indoors, I decided it was time to see what it was like outside. Flying an X12 outside left something to be desired, so I began researching to figure out what might fit the bill. After reading MANY reviews and watching a ton of videos, I chose the X5c. It fit my budget, and I got the impression that it truly was a great quad to learn on.

Well, after only a few short months of owning it I can say with certainty that the X5 has certainly held up its end of the bargain, and then some. I say "X5", and not X5"c", because the camera that comes with this thing is pretty lame. The angle (or field of vision, if you prefer) is very narrow. And I don't know if this is simply an issue with Macs, but I had to reformat the SD-card all the time- simply deleting files didn't work. Otherwise, the camera would believe that there wasn't enough space on the card and wouldn't record. So, this made it very easy for me to make the decision to jettison the camera all together, and just let this bird fly free. And I didn't stop there... the feet were no longer necessary either, so away they went too. The prop guards? Never even bothered attaching them to begin with. Flying this thing was kinda fun before getting rid of that stuff, but it became much more fun without the extra baggage.

From the beginning, I chose to learn on "advanced mode", just because it was faster, more responsive, and more challenging. However, I was by no means "advanced" at flying these things. The first time I took it anyplace that wasn't my tiny front yard, I took it to a local park and flew it up kinda high. Well, then I experienced that common thing where you kinda get disoriented with where the quad is in relation to nearby trees, and somehow I flew it into some woods with it impacting the first few branches at around 50 feet. Somehow, by some miracle, the thing didn't get hung up in any of those branches- I'm attributing that to the fact that it was still winter time (not many leaves to help hold it there)... so, where does it ultimately land? Where else, than in a creek? Yup! Brand new lil quad... in the creek. I just took a big deep breath and hung my head when I realized this. Somehow the thing was still on when I fished it out (it never completely submerged- landed in shallow area). I immediately turned it off and removed the battery before shaking it out best I could. Then I brought it home, opened it up, and placed it on the floor about a foot away from a space heater to allow it to dry out for the rest of the day. The next morning, I put everything back together, popped the recharged battery back in, and everything worked perfectly. From then on, I became much more careful about flying at any sort of altitude that included potential trees... and creeks, for that matter. It also didn't take me long to see the need for more batteries. I bought one of the packages available here on Amazon, where it provides you with four batteries and a 4x1 charger to charge them all simultaneously. I also bought to extra batteries before getting the 4x1. So, now that I have 7 batteries, I find myself not only enjoying the thing more, personally, I also have found more time to teach others how to fly it.

O, and before I forget... another sad, yet awesome, thing that happened: I was on my way to go begin my marathon of marathon study sessions for finals when I stopped by at a nearby church to catch about 10 minutes of flight time. I parked in a different area than usual so that I could see what range I could accomplish, and then flew it back with more altitude and speed than I'd intended.... well, I didn't turn fast enough and right behind me was a nice tree waiting to catch the quad. It got stuck at probably 40 feet up. I found various things laying around to throw at it, and even when I hit it with a lightweight block of wood, the thing still didn't budge. I climbed as high as I could, but the branches became too thin and there was no one around to spot me if I fell. Not worth it. So, I just had to let it be. I thought to myself... o well, you need to study anyway. This thing was obviously only meant to be an ill-fated distraction. So I went on my way and decided that I'd re-evaluate the situation only after I'd gotten through at least half of the material I needed to cover. So, a week and several thunderstorms later, I returned to the scene to find the quad stil sitting up in the tree looking all happy. I devised a telescoping "pushstick" made out of an 8' cardboard tube and some quarter round. I tied a rope to it, climbed the tree as high as I could, and then managed to push the quad out of the tree after extending the "pushstick" to a length of almost 20 feet. Took the quad home, opened it up, and it was bone dry and with no signs of rust of weathering. I put it all back together, and it worked. No problems at all. It's amazing.

I've crashed this thing into everything except for myself or other people. I've let my dog chase it, and eventually she even got ahold of it. Still, the quad survives. It slammed into a road sign at full speed earlier today. It survives. I've put this thing through tons of punishment, and thus far, the only thing I've needed to replace is two of those tiny cogs/gears at the bottom of the motor (the ones that engage with the larger gears that actually spin the props). These smaller gears seem to have a tendency to slip over time, and then they fall off. I've gotten into the habit of performing a little flight check before each flight, and confirming that those are properly seated seems to have made a big difference. Still, I have extras now. In anticipation of eventually burning out a motor, I also went ahead and purchased an extra CW and CCW motor. The nice thing about the prospect of changing out the motors is that the new ones have a metal gear that seems like it won't slip like the little plastic ones do. I dunno; we'll see.

I know I'll eventually destroy this thing, but OMG it blows my mind how much it's been through and is still going strong. I'd post a picture of how beat up it is, but I'm afraid it wouldn't really do it justice. It's scratched all over, one of the props was bent and then reshapaned before getting chewed on by my friend's cat. Still, the quad survives...

Once I finally burn out a motor or somehow destroy this thing, I'll update my review to let you know how it goes. Overall, I'm getting a lot of good times out of it. Still learning new ways to enjoy it. Definitely the start of a new hobby.
text_fidelity_b: Syma X5C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Explorers Quad Copter w/ Camera

They are bright with a variety of colors including black and white. Crayola has never come across as a high-end brand, but in oil pastels they are highly regarded as some of the best, and I agree. If you watch some of the videos on YouTube about how to use oil pastels you will realize how great these are. You can also see comparison videos, and the crayola brand gets very high marks. Oil pastels don't make a mess unless you use your finger to blend them, and then your finger will be a big mess. But you can clean it with baby wipes or soap and water or lotion to get down into your skin if it's dry. You can use traditional rolled paper sticks for blending also. These come packaged neatly so you can keep them in their original slots in that packaging. Besides coloring with them you can also use a wet brush to blend them, and you can layer them on top of each other or blend them together with your finger. I have also seen them covered with a clear acrylic paint and then used again on top of that paint. You can see that on YouTube. These are an inexpensive way to enjoy yourself artistically and produce beautiful results just like painting when you add the water or vodka or a blender like turpenoid.

QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits

Hot Wheels Race Crate with 3 Stunts in 1 Set Portable Storage Ages 6 to 10 Adult review: it's fast. So fast it's over before it starts. I was most interested in the 4 lane gravity drop and it works perfectly. People complaining cars won't loop may not be trying different cars. After picking different cars a few times I have several that loop correctly. The two that came with it also loop correctly. Some of the longer cars don't seem to make it.

This is one of the neatest designs I've ever seen from Hot Wheels. If you wanted the 6 lane kit that's over 200 dollars from scalpers now...this is a pretty great one to settle for. My only complaints on the gravity drop are it's so fast it's really hard to watch and if you're at the starting end...the large solid loop prevents you from seeing the cars until the hit the finish line. If the loop were clear that would be awesome. I also added some old '68 track and will add more....the cars clear the finish with lots of go power left. Add more track :)

I ended up liking the drag race configuration best with added track.

I believe it is sturdy and it's a pretty big track in any configuration. The fact it all folds into itself for storage is the truly awesome part. Room for several cars in there as well.

Good product for young and old Hot Wheels fans and I wish it had been cheaper but feel I got my money's worth. If kids don't lose any of the few loose pieces....I would imagine it will hold value.

LEGO Creator 3in1 Twin Rotor Helicopter 31096 Building Kit (569 Pieces) One of these things is not like the others. The boat is pretty standard, as is the airplane. The Helicopter is all kinds of cool. The twin rotor blades spin, the hatch in back opens, and the winch is capable of lifting the buoy that comes with the kit.

It's an interesting way to put together a 3 in one kit. We built the helicopter first. It's the most difficult build in the box, uses the most pieces, has the most complexity, and is far and away the nicest looking model. Then we took that apart to build the rather uninspiring "super fast plane" and the "awesome hovercraft" that looks just like a chubby boat. You do not have the pieces in here to build all three at once and play with them together.

It's certainly nice to have a very cool model like this, and I love that there are kits nowadays that utilize the multiple instructions. I wish that the other models were a little more in line with the helicopter.

text_fidelity_a: Nerf N-Strike Elite Firestrike This is my first external cocking blaster and I'm in awe of its range and accuracy.  Flat, in the house shots, are going from my kitchen, down the hall, and thru the family room and hitting the wall (45 feet!).  This is by far as well as my Rampage does. Accuracy is also superb.  I wasn't sure that such little cocking force was going to be able to shoot darts so far or fast.  This little gem will fire elite darts and whistlers.  It does not like streamlines and the suction cup darts.  The bullseye LED target light works pretty good in the dark, and seem to be accurate enough to nail a human size target at 30 feet.  I love the way the 2 spare dart holders seem to blend into the overall scheme of the blaster.  Hurray for nerf for attaching these to the packaging with easy to cut twine, rather than the usual zipties.  The included darts work in all blasters but are easily lost (especially when this blaster shoots them so far) so be sure to pick up extras (I use the Elite dart in all my blasters so I get the 75 pack to replace all the lost ones).  Please be careful when shooting poeple as a shot to the face can be surprisingly painful.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Firestrike

They call them “MINIS” for a reason. .. they are small. They are about 2” long and about 1.5” tall. This means they can be easily lost. . . stepped on. . . and perhaps even sucked-up in a vacuum. So you’ll want to make sure you store them properly.

It shows that this product is for ages three and up. I’m not sure I totally agree. Again, the “MINIS” are small, and could be a choking hazard of if you have child who likes to put everything in their mouth. As long as that’s not an issue, then you should be fine.

This track is bright and colorful. It’s more of a “vertical” sort of item, so it doesn’t take-up too much space.

text_fidelity_a:
Nerf Official: Lazer Tag Phoenix LTX Tagger 2-pack - Fun Multiplayer Laser Tag Game for Kids & Adults, Ages 8 & Up (Amazon Exclusive) I was skeptical about playing with laser tag guns. I'm an adult and the ones we had as a kid sucked. These are different. There is recoil when you shoot. When you run out of ammo you have to physically reload the gun, a pop the clip out and put a new clip in motion. We thought that one pair of the guns (we got two sets) was defective. Turns out we are just idiots and had 2 of the 4 the guns set to outside mode. That makes the guns far more vulnerable to getting hit as outside mode is for over longer distances (to the point where we were shooting at the ceiling with the gun going off like it was a direct hit). Once we had all the guns set to indoor mode it corrected the problem and it was extremely accurate.

These turned out to be a lot of fun and we are ordering another pair today!
text_fidelity_b: Nerf Official: Lazer Tag Phoenix LTX Tagger 2-pack - Fun Multiplayer Laser Tag Game for Kids & Adults, Ages 8 & Up (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
GLÜCK 2-in-1 Ride and Walker Toy Sit to Stand Toddler Ride On Toy for Toddlers and Babies Aged 18 Months to 3Years Very cute! The only assembly required is easily popping the handle into place and inserting two AA batteries. The toy is colorful and rolls well. The handle has two buttons to activate the music and noises. One button will beep the horn and make a couple of other noises; the other button plays a few different tunes. The music isn’t overly loud, not as loud as with some toys, but I learned long ago that if sounds get too loud, a piece of packing tape over the speaker solves that problem by drastically reducing the volume.
A good ride-on toy for young children learning to use their feet to move on their own.
text_fidelity_b: GLÜCK 2-in-1 Ride and Walker Toy Sit to Stand Toddler Ride On Toy for Toddlers and Babies Aged 18 Months to 3Years

text_fidelity_a: Rubik's Hasbro Gaming Cube 3 x 3 Puzzle Game for Kids Ages 8 and Up I have several of these and the book Speed Solving the Cube. All I can say is that I have played with other cubes now and they do not have the feel and the reputation of the original Rubik's Cube. If you are wanting to keep your brain moving and exercise your hands and fingers, this is the way to go. You would really be surprised at how easy it is to learn how to solve these. I have not done it faster than 60 seconds , and I do not think I ever will. Only because my hands and fingers are not able to move that fast. You can see the moves, just cant get them there. Ha
text_fidelity_b: Rubik's Hasbro Gaming Cube 3 x 3 Puzzle Game for Kids Ages 8 and Up
